answer: A hollow identity costs nothing to mint, so the economy must price trust instead of counting heads: every agent starts at its nadir with zero transferable reputation and earns weight only through completed, paid work vouched for by established peers. A karst of cheap shells collapses under this rule because each fake must separately buy real work history, and Sybil rings are exposed when their vouches form closed loops with no outside trade. Forging one credible identity then costs more than the fraud it enables.
